lead.t: Acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) is a subtype that is more common in certain regions of the world, but the incidence of the other types is generally uniform.

snip.t: Acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) is a subtype that is more common in certain regions of the world, but the incidence of the other types is generally uniform.
Targeted agents – ATRA for acute promyelocytic leukemia; arsenic trioxide for same; FLT3 inhibitors for FLT3‑mutated AML; BCR‑ABL TKIs for Ph‑positive ALL/CML.
*Answer*: “7 + 3” induction (anthracycline + cytarabine) plus ATRA because of Auer rods suggesting acute promyelocytic leukemia.
APL with PML-RARA  (Acute promyelocytic leukemia with promyelocytic leukemia–retinoic acid receptor alpha)

qs.q: A 52-year-old woman with acute promyelocytic leukemia develops profound coagulopathy and sudden onset cyanosis with severe hypoxemia. Which organ system involvement best explains these pulmonary findings?
o: Central nervous system involvement with thrombosis
Respiratory system involvement with microvascular clots
Cardiovascular system involvement with heart failure
Renal system involvement with acute tubular necrosis
qs.e: Respiratory system involvement in disseminated intravascular coagulation can present with cyanosis and respiratory failure due to microvascular thrombosis. CNS involvement typically presents with focal deficits or altered mental status rather than acute hypoxemia.
